title: Chapter 1 Quiz 6
description: A mixed review of Chapter 1. This time, say how sure you are.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: Which of these is **not** required of an algorithm?
options: It must give at least one result
It must always need an input
It must end after a finite number of steps
questions.explanation: An algorithm may or may not need input. It must be finite, definite and give at least one output.

questions.question: A program that runs but gives wrong results has a syntax error.
questions.explanation: Wrong results from a program that runs point to a semantic (design) error. Syntax errors stop the program from running at all.

questions.question: Match each symbol to its function.
Place the shapes on the flowchart that tests whether a number is positive.
questions.explanation: Input and output are parallelograms, and the question x > 0 ? is a diamond.

questions.question: Using coefficients 3, 2 and 5, grades 8, 12 and 10, find (8×3 + 12×2 + 10×5) / (3 + 2 + 5).
A {{1}} error is reported by the {{2}}, and no executable program is produced.
questions.explanation: Syntax errors break the rules of the language, so the compiler cannot translate the program.

questions.question: Which stages are done automatically by the machine?
questions.explanation: Analysis and coding are human work. Compilation and running are automatic.
